_comment: Anti-drift vectors for the GET /api/fleet contract (tvos/discovery/DISCOVERY.md).
Each vector's `input` is the exact body a source serves, as a string so the bytes
are pinned; `normalized` is the snapshot the Wall's Rust core must hand Swift for
it. tvos/witness-core/tests/fleet_contract.rs reads this file. The contract doc
changes first, then this file, then the code — never the other way around.
The first vector pins the one default the doc and both decoders used to disagree
on: a device that omits `online` is NOT claimed present (`online: false`).
A vector may also carry `born`: per normalized row, the birth-day line every reader
renders ({label, utc_date}) or null for none. A vector without it draws no line on
any row. Born appears only when born_exact is true; a day without that is First dated.

vectors.name: a silent `online` is not a presence claim
the bare array form, with `online` silent on every row
a display's own self-report bytes (fleet_selfreport_build, verbatim)
an explicit `online: false` survives, and an explicit `true` is not the default talking

a display's aggregated body carries the wellbeing keys through, and a row without them stays silent (fleet_selfreport open/append/close, verbatim — the same literal the iPhone's FleetSelfReportTests.aggregatedBody pins)
vectors._note: The Rust Device used to end at `hub`, and serde strips unknown fields — so presence/occupants/breathing/seeing/seeing_score vanished here before Swift ever saw them. The self row carries none of the keys and none may be invented: absence is 'cannot say', never an empty calm room. (`chain_height` is not part of this normalizer's shape and does not survive it — a change to that is a contract change, made in DISCOVERY.md first.)

vectors.name: unknown wellbeing words survive as words — tolerance lives in the reader, not in this normalizer
vectors._note: A word this build has never sent must cross intact so the client can fold it to 'cannot say'; stripping or rewriting it here would turn a future firmware's honest claim into silence or a guess. The out-of-range score crosses too — what counts as a percentage is the reader's call, same as what counts as a known word.

vectors.name: the kernel's aggregated document (fleet_document, verbatim): itself plus one Canary the bridge heard
vectors._note: The repo-root kernel's own /api/fleet bytes for one planted peer (src/api tests, fleet_document_matches_the_shared_two_row_vector): its self row first, then the Canary its MQTT bridge heard — named from the retained meta topic, `online` proven by a signed chain publish 30 s before the snapshot against the key pinned for it, the room words fresh. The kernel side pins `input` byte-for-byte and this side pins `normalized`, so neither can move the two-row shape alone. Nothing the bridge keeps privately (the pinned key, the device id, timestamps) appears in `input` — the second test below asserts that.

vectors.name: a Canary born the evening it was set up: its day and the word Born (fleet_selfreport_build, verbatim — the iPhone's FleetSelfReportTests.bornBody)
vectors._note: born_day is days since the Unix epoch, a UTC day with no time of day (firmware/common/identity/birth_day.h); born_exact true means the device met a clock while its key was still fresh. `born` says what every reader must render for each row: the label and the UTC calendar day, or null for no line at all.

vectors.name: a Canary that met a clock late says First dated, never Born (fleet_selfreport_build, verbatim — the iPhone's FleetSelfReportTests.firstDatedBody)
vectors._note: A Canary that sat on a shelf before it ever saw a network records the day it was first DATED and says so with born_exact false. Same kind of number, a different claim: a reader that dropped the flag would promote a week on a shelf into a birthday.

vectors.name: no birth day, or half a pair: absence is 'cannot say', a day without its flag is not a birthday, and a flag without a day dates nothing
vectors._note: The firmware writes born_day and born_exact together or not at all, so the second and third rows come from no firmware this repo builds. The normalizer carries each half as sent and the reader decides: a missing flag reads as not exact (the flag exists to hold a claim back), and a flag with no day draws nothing.

vectors.name: a birth day of the wrong type is dropped, never fatal: the row and the rest of the snapshot survive
vectors._note: A string, a fraction, a null, an array or an object is not a day, and anything but true/false is not the flag. Each is dropped to absent rather than failing the parse, because a failed parse loses the WHOLE snapshot and one strange row would blank the Wall for every device that answered. Rows K and L put a good day beside a flag that only looks true (the string "true", the number 1): the day crosses, the flag does not, and the line reads First dated, never Born, so a reader that tests the flag for truthiness instead of for true goes red here.

vectors.name: a day no Canary can stamp is not a date: 0 is the firmware's own 'never dated', and the window runs from its clock floor (2025-01-01) to the last day a 32-bit clock names (2106-02-07)
vectors._note: The firmware stamps only a believable clock (kClockFloor in birth_day.h: day 20089) and its clock is a uint32_t count of seconds (at most day 49710), so a day outside 20089..=49710 came from no Canary. The day is dropped and the flag beside it crosses alone, which a reader renders as nothing. The two edges themselves are days.
